doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Rehearsal band, Norvo and Mildred Bailey, and the Famous Door
summary: Brick Fleagle's band led to the Norvo job, with Zarchy and Zudekoff in the trumpet section, until the Famous Door let the big band go at Christmas.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: The union, yeah. Because it would be a union job, and your name would go into the records and so forth and so on. Anyway, the day I got my card, there was a band that I was rehearsing with. It was what they call a rehearsal band. Musicians came in from out of town, and then somebody heard them and they went with a band on the road, or things, it was one of those kind of bands. Brick Fleegle. And I was in that band and George Wettling heard me. And he says, “You know Red Norvo and Mildred Bailey?” And I said, “Well I heard of them.” He says, “You available?” I says, “Yeah.” He says, “Why don’t you make a rehearsal at Carnegie Hall, somewhere around that studio.” And he says, “Will you be there?” And I says, “Yeah.” He says, “All right, then I won’t look for anybody else.” So I went there and there was Red Norvo and Mildred Bailey and I sat down and there was Zeke Zarchy playing first trumpet, and Barney Zudekoff was Moe Zudekoff’s brother. So there was Zeke Zarchy playing lead, I played second in the hot chair, and Barney Zudicoff played third trumpet. Those were the three trumpets. Wow. Good band too.
Oh, yeah, those were the days.
And how long did you stay in New York?

Well the band broke up at The Famous Door. We went to The Famous Door and it was around Christmas time — what a time to be let go, right? And the two bosses, Mutt and Jeff we called them because one was a big guy and the other one was shorty. They decided they couldn’t afford to have the band during the Christmas holidays. So they let the band, the big band go, and they just kept Red Norvo and Mildred Bailey, and three other musicians. And John Kirby’s quintet was the alternate band. So that was it. So there I was out of work right? So then incidentally, going in and out of the subway, Jerry Jerome and make the Harry James rehearsal which I did, and from there it was pretty good.
